comparisons.title: Same goal. Different heating strategies.
comparisons.goal: Heat a mug and put it in a cabinet.

changes.label: Heating strategy
changes.right: Uses the microwave, then the cabinet

comparisons.interpretation: These are separate C and E evaluations of the same task instance. The microwave route appears in E's plan; the shown rule concerns navigation after heating. This pair illustrates behavior, not the isolated effect of that rule.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: One goal, the same restored scene
beats.text: Both recorded policies must heat a mug and store it in a cabinet.

beats.label: Pick up
beats.title: Both agents obtain the mug
beats.text: The difference emerges after pickup, rather than from whether the mug can be found.

beats.label: Decision
beats.title: The routes diverge
beats.text: C goes to a stoveburner. E goes to the microwave.

beats.label: Heat
beats.title: A failed placement versus a valid heating command
beats.text: C attempts an invalid placement on a stoveburner. E executes heat mug 1 with microwave 1.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: The outcomes separate
beats.text: C uses the full 30-action budget without heating the mug. E satisfies the goal in eight actions.

comparisons.title: Same goal. Fourteen actions versus three.
comparisons.goal: Hold the bowl with the desk lamp turned on.

changes.label: Handling the bowl
changes.left: Puts it down, then repeatedly examines the desk
changes.right: Keeps holding it and switches on the lamp

comparisons.interpretation: Both evaluations succeed on the exact same task instance. The visible difference is efficiency: C takes 11 additional actions. The simulator's goal requires holding the bowl with the lamp on; repeated examine commands are unnecessary.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same bowl and lamp task
beats.text: The objective is satisfied when the agent is holding the bowl and the desk lamp is on.

beats.label: Pick up
beats.title: Both pick up the bowl
beats.text: At this point both policies have the object needed for the goal.

beats.label: Decision
beats.title: C puts it down; E turns on the lamp
beats.text: E completes the task. C has put the bowl back on the desk, so turning the lamp on next is insufficient.

beats.label: Extra work
beats.title: E is finished while C keeps examining
beats.text: C repeatedly examines the desk with empty hands. E's completed replay holds its final frame.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: Both win, with an 11-action difference
beats.text: C eventually picks the bowl up again with the lamp already on. E reaches that state directly in three actions.

comparisons.title: Same task. A failed attempt, then a successful retry.
comparisons.goal: Find the cloth and put it in a drawer.

changes.label: Prompt context
changes.left: No reflection from this attempt yet
changes.right: Reflection on the failed search is supplied

changes.label: Rule manual during the attempt
changes.right: The manual stays fixed during the retry

comparisons.interpretation: This is a genuine chronological first-attempt/retry sequence for one practice game. Reflection is added before the retry. The Builder writes a new Success Process after the retry succeeds; that new rule did not cause this retry's win.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same practice game is reset
beats.text: Both attempts begin from the same task scene and need to find a cloth for the drawer.

beats.label: Reflect
beats.title: Failure produces a reflection
beats.text: The first attempt ends without finding the cloth. Its reflection is supplied when the retry starts.

beats.label: Find cloth
beats.title: The retry finds and picks up the cloth
beats.text: The retry searches several receptacles, finds the cloth at the toilet, and takes it.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: The retry succeeds and the Builder records a procedure
beats.text: After placing the cloth in the drawer, the Builder adds a new Success Process to the rule manual.
